text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia and Slovakia reach agreement on abolishing visas to be signed after confirmation by the two governments.
- Serb government in Eastern Slavonia urges Serb population to collectively ask for issuance of Croatian citizenship papers according to population list from 1991.
- Serbian government agrees to release 10,000 tonnes of flour from commodity reserves to supply bakeries.
- Director of statistical office Milovan Zivkovic expects Yugoslavia to return to the IMF and the World Trade Organisation by end of June.
- Payments office Wednesday finally informed the JIK bank of its closure according to National Bank of Yugoslavia decision from January 24.
- Foreign exchange rate cannot be changed, said Serbian minister coordinator Dragan Tomic.
- Belgrade-based Balkan Lawyers' Association for Criminal set up on Wednesday.
- Tourism industry expected to grow by 20 percent in 1997 despite its 3.7 percent fall in 1996 compared to the year earlier, says Tourism Minister Mira Stankovic.
- There are 600 schools in Serbia in strike over social demands, says president of the Serbian education trade union Jagos Bulatovic.
- Normalisation of education in Kosovo expected soon, write papers in Kosovo without giving specific details.
- No Yugoslav Army troops are being sent to reinforce police cordons, says the army in a statement stressing its neutral position.
NASA BORBA
- Opposition representatives Zoran Djindjic, Vojin Dimitrijevic and Milan Bozic are to attend the international economic forum in Davos.
- Students marched through Belgrade streets without being obstructed by police. Zajedno opposition supporters also held another rally in the centre of town over annulment of election results.
- Ten Vojvodina political parties and 13 non party organisations signed a proposal to change constitutional position of Vojvodina and restore its autonomy.
- Farmers will not make agreements about spring sowing before the government pays its dues for autumn crops.
- Student protest information service denies claims the students urged introduction of sanctions against Yugoslavia during their visit to Washington.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- According to unconfirmed information, Serbian government to replace ministers of education, Dragoslav Mladenovic, private enterprise Radoje Djukic and tourism Mirjana Stankovic, abolish information ministry and set up function of spokesman which will be held by Miodrag Popovic. Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic expected to stay.
- Newspaper unofficially learns about ten people from the secret organisation National Movement for the Liberation of Kosovo arrested.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Yugoslavia was on verge of being received into the World Trade Organisation but current political developments delayed the decision, says Yugoslav Trade Minister Djordje Siradovic.
- new management of Electricity Company of Serbia EPS, expected to make more changes in company's top, paper learns.
- National Bank of Yugoslavia agrees to extend 140 million mark loan to pay outstanding debts to medicine factories.
